summary.name: Federated identity
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing federated identity, the practice of linking a person's electronic identity and attributes across separate identity management systems so they can be used across organizations.
use_cases: Understanding how single sign-on works across organizations
Choosing identity standards for cross-domain login
Enabling social login on third-party websites
Researching identity federation in research and education
summary.what_it_does: The page explains federated identity as linking a person's electronic identity and attributes stored across multiple identity management systems. It describes how single sign-on relates to federation as a subset focused on authentication. It lists standards and technologies used for federation, including SAML, OAuth, OpenID, and JSON Web Tokens. It also gives examples of social login providers such as Google Account, Microsoft account, GitHub, and PayPal, and notes government initiatives like NIST and FedRAMP.
notable: Explains the relationship between federated identity and single sign-on (SSO)
Lists open standards such as SAML, OAuth, and OpenID
Notes Mozilla Persona services were shut down on November 30, 2016
caveats: Encyclopedia article, not a software tool; it describes concepts rather than a product
Parts of the page are flagged as needing more citations
Some example services listed, such as Mozilla Persona, have been discontinued
